header_summary:
A new protocol synthesizing elements from existing consensus mechanisms has been proposed to enable soft-agreement on transaction batches within the Bitcoin mempool, resulting in faster block propagation and improved network efficiency. Full technical details and specifications are provided in the research paper available [here](https://beige-worrying-unicorn-969.mypinata.cloud/ipfs/bafybeigsbdid4znwtmoqh55yid2etxkujci33dzqt3ia6bt5vwsnllfqym) ([source](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/snowball-to-snowstorm/3014)).

Recent network anomalies were traced to a series of chained runestone mint transactions utilizing P2A inputs and OP_RETURN outputs, which were directly broadcast to peers via unsolicited `tx` messages, bypassing standard relay protocols. Subsequent burning of "anyone-can-spend" outputs by third parties led to significant mempool inconsistencies and compact block reconstruction degradation until the cessation of these activities on October 18, 2026, as discussed in detail at [bnoc.xyz](https://bnoc.xyz/t/satoshi-31-0-0-peers-with-no-service-flags-and-protocol-70015-pushed-transactions-then-stopped-together-on-oct-18/193/) and [here](https://bnoc.xyz/t/compact-block-reconstruction-degradation-between-september-october-2026/198/) ([source](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/stats-on-compact-block-reconstructions/1052/63)).

A comparative analysis of three eltoo-style channel implementations—APO+CTV, CSFS+CTV rekey ladder, and the latest TEMPLATEHASH+CSFS+INTERNALKEY—highlights advances in script efficiency, transaction count, and witness size. The recent TEMPLATEHASH approach, detailed by Aaron van Wirdum and collaborators, demonstrates a streamlined update process and flexible scripting, with technical documentation and reproducible code available at [`templatehash.py`](https://github.com/aaron-recompile/btcaaron/blob/5ef4cb3dff5d51d812ff55a134d48c0e269323e7/btcaaron/templatehash.py) ([source](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/eltoo-state-chain-on-signet-third-time-templatehash-csfs-internalkey/3012)).

recent_posts.title: Snowball to Snowstorm
recent_posts.summary: - A new protocol enables soft-agreement in the Bitcoin mempool before blocks are discovered.  - It achieves batch agreement using elements from various consensus mechanisms, resembling the Snowball protocol.  - Coordinated transaction selection improves efficiency and streamlines block formation and network propagation.

recent_posts.title: Stats on compact block reconstructions
recent_posts.summary: - A cost-efficient minting strategy used compact P2A and OP_RETURN transactions, chained together in succession.  - Unsolicited transmission and swift burning of outputs induced mempool inconsistencies and network propagation irregularities.  - The cessation of these transaction chains on October 18, 2026, led to improved block reconstruction metrics.

recent_posts.title: Eltoo state chain on signet, third time: TEMPLATEHASH + CSFS + INTERNALKEY
recent_posts.summary: - Three distinct channel methods were implemented: APO+CTV, CSFS+CTV ladder, and TEMPLATEHASH+CSFS+INTERNALKEY.  - Comparative analysis covered transaction counts, witness sizes, update leaf sizes, and scripting simplicity.  - Technical distinctions focused on their interaction with Bitcoin’s script interpreter and resulting scripting flexibility.

active_posts.title: Stats on compact block reconstructions
active_posts.summary: - Compact block reconstruction efficiency depends on transaction availability and node configuration across the Bitcoin network.  - Configuration changes, such as increased connections or enabling full-RBF, significantly influence block reconstruction outcomes.  - Reconstruction performance varies with mempool activity, hardware, and additional transaction requests, prompting further study.

active_posts.title: Eltoo state chain on signet, third time: TEMPLATEHASH + CSFS + INTERNALKEY
active_posts.summary: - Three different state channel constructions were compared: APO+CTV, CSFS+CTV ladder, and TEMPLATEHASH-based scripts.  - TEMPLATEHASH enabled smaller update scripts, constant witness sizes, and improved transaction efficiency and flexibility.  - Technical comparison revealed distinct scripting behaviors and architectural simplifications unique to each implementation method.

active_posts.title: Snowball to Snowstorm
active_posts.summary: - A protocol accelerates Bitcoin mempool soft-agreement to improve transaction processing and block creation.  - It enables batch agreement on transaction sets, enhancing coordination and reducing redundancies in selection.  - Technical details and specifications are available via the provided link and content identifier.

today_in_history_posts.title: BIP- & SLIP-0039 -- better multi-language support
today_in_history_posts.summary: - BIP-0039 is criticized for its language dependence, especially regarding mnemonic sentence generation.  - Guo suggests mnemonic codes should represent entropy, with third-party tools handling language translation.  - He proposes allowing seeds to be represented as decimal numbers for users lacking native language support.

today_in_history_posts.title: Wireshark plug-in for Lightning Network(BOLT) protocol
today_in_history_posts.summary: - The Nayuta team is creating a Wireshark plug-in to decode Lightning Network BOLT messages.  - They suggest a compile option in implementations to output key information files for decoding.  - The goal is to standardize log formats, improving interoperability testing among Lightning Network implementations.

today_in_history_posts.title: Batched Splicing Considered Risky
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Splicing transactions in the Lightning Network introduce vulnerabilities due to the lack of disruption disincentives.  - Malicious actors can exploit these vulnerabilities, causing operational risks and potential losses for channel participants.  - Proposed mitigations carry added complexity and do not fully resolve the increased risk in batched splicing scenarios.
